properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 12:14AM MST until August 24 at 1:30AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
At 1214 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated a couple of rounds of
thunderstorms last night had produced between 1.00 and 3.50 inches of
heavy rain along and east of Route 15 between Santa Rosa and North
Komelik. The heaviest rainfall, between 2.50 and 3.50 inches,
occurred near and east of North Komelik. Flash flooding is ongoing,
especially in normally dry washes and low-lying areas that drain into
the Santa Rosa Wash.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Komelik.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Santa Rosa Wash, Anegam Wash and Sil Nakya Wash.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 23 at 1:17PM CDT until August 29 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Paducah has issued a Flood Warning
for the following river in Illinois...Indiana...

Wabash River at New Harmony.

.Heavy rainfall last week continues to cause slow rises on the Wabash
River.  At New Harmony, the river is forecast to climb above flood
stage Tuesday, and crest just under a foot above flood stage
Thursday.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning to Saturday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday morning to a crest of 15.8 feet early Thursday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Wills Creek at Cambridge.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

feet on 02/18/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Mobile.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 23 at 9:53PM EDT until August 28 at 11:20PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following river and
location in Indiana...

White River at Elliston, Edwardsport, and Hazleton.


...The Flood Warning continues for the following river and locations
in Indiana...

White River at Newberry and Petersburg.

.On the White River, minor flooding continues, with a broad crest
between Edwardsport and Hazleton as of Sunday evening. Flooding is
predicted to end on the White River Friday afternoon.

Largely dry weather is in store for the week, with a 50 percent or
less chance of rain Wednesday afternoon and night.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...White River at Hazleton.

* WHEN...Until late Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Most of the low bottomlands flood.
Flooding begins in higher bottomlands. High water affects any
residents in Pottsville river cabins. Pottsville Road...North C
Street on river side of railroad tracks and Catt Street near U.S.
Highway 41 are flooded. Water is near or starting on Giro Road in
the vicinity of submerged Pottsville Road. Oil stripped fields
flood. Flood gates must be installed at Hazleton.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is no current observed data.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.6
feet Wednesday morning. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths
occur in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges,
dips, or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream,
even a small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route
over higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued Monday afternoon by around 200
PM EDT /100 PM CDT/.
